guarantees: Adds last_restore_at metadata without changing document revisions.
Adds owner_sub metadata with the local owner as its stable default.
Adds temporal relationship state and optional death-moment references.
Adds a primary time system without changing the figures revision.
Adds indexed entity-alias persistence without changing the figures revision.
Migrates the legacy empty owner_sub sentinel to quiltor-internal:local-owner without changing document revisions.
Adds normalized optional chapter story-time moment and range references without changing chapter order or document revisions.
Adds a recursive manuscript binder and migrates every existing chapter to the root without changing chapter identity, order, prose, or document revisions.
Adds stable figure-profile field identities and migrates every non-empty legacy fixed or custom profile value without changing figure identity, notes, references, or document revisions.
Adds an independently revisioned non-canon Storyboard document and one stable default Main Storyboard without changing manuscript, story-world, or existing world data.

Adds content-addressed storage for place map images inside the world database, so that backup, history, and restore carry them without a manifest change, and without touching document revisions or existing world data.

Renames the two manuscript settings that still carried German keys: the hidden insert-panel elements move from `elementeVerborgen` to `hiddenElements` inside the settings' passthrough bag, and any stale `zeichenAktiv` left in that bag is dropped because the active symbols live in their own column. Runs when a world is opened, leaves document revisions untouched, and is a no-op for a world that never stored either key.

Renames the last two German keys inside stored assistant responses, where a proposal that is still applicable kept the spelling it was written in: `notizen` becomes `notes` and `gerichtet` becomes `directed`, an already present English key wins, and only object keys are touched so the German prose these answers cite stays as it is. Runs when a world is opened, leaves document revisions and every other table untouched, and is a no-op for a world whose history never carried either key.

Gives every element one note: the text of each Storyboard reference card is appended to the note of the chapter, figure, place or timeline moment it shows, as a block `

— Aus Storyboard „<board title>“ —
<text>` (without the leading blank paragraph when the element note is empty), ordered by board position, card position and card id, one block per card without deduplication; blank card texts append nothing. Note references and marks move with their text, shifted by the block offset in UTF-16 code units, and a reference id that is already taken on the target note gets the first free suffix `-sb1`, `-sb2`, ....

Afterwards no reference card carries text, note references or note marks. A card whose element is missing (deleted figure or moment, chapter in the trash) or whose block would exceed a note limit (chapter note 100000 characters, 10000 references or marks) loses its text; such cards are counted per board and element in `meta.migration_v15_discarded_notes`, never with their text. A figure without a profile row gets one.

Deterministic and idempotent, so a migrated cloud snapshot and the world it restores have the same fingerprint. Advances `storyboards_revision`, and `manuscript_revision` or `figures_revision`, only when that document changed; a meta-only database is left alone. The markdown mirror is refreshed on the next save, not by this step.

Adds the column `engine` to `assistant_interactions`, so the audit names the kind of engine that computed an answer (`server`, `webllm` or `cloud`), never a model name or a key. Every interaction recorded before reads `server`, the column's default, because only the server engine existed. Runs when a world is opened, checks `sqlite_master` first and does nothing for a database without the table, leaves document revisions and every other table untouched, and is idempotent.
